how_the_600_instances_get_checked.principle: None of them is edited. Every one is an INSTANCE of 2041:19568 or 2041:19571, and both node ids survive the rename — a variant rename changes the property vocabulary the set reports, not the node an instance points at. So all 600 inherit the corrected active treatment from one master edit, and zero board edits land inside sections 01-27 that twelve other agents are holding.
how_the_600_instances_get_checked.why_not_a_new_set: Building a better set beside the old one and swapping 600 instances would be both a duplicate master (the thing this job exists to prevent) and 600 edits inside other agents' write scope.
how_the_600_instances_get_checked.the_check: node scripts/figma/instance-map.mjs 2041:19572 --page=1:3 --ids=6 — written for this plan, not yet run. It matches on the SET id AND every variant id under it, because an instance resolves to a variant and never to the set; asking a set for its own instance count returns zero for every set in the file. Output is per-section counts (complete) plus a bounded sample of node ids per section (capped, and it says so) — 600 ids do not fit in one MCP result, and a truncated list has already been read as a short list once in this arc.
acceptance: instance-map total on page 1:3 equals the pre-merge total for the same master (no instance detached or orphaned)
every returned instance resolves to 2041:19568 or 2041:19571 — no instance points at one of the four NEW variants, because nothing was swapped
verify-invariants.mjs reports no new board overlap in section 2040:8372 (the set grows from 140x30 to 792x112 and the plan restacks the three sets vertically off the Rail to prevent exactly that)
a render of any one Settings board shows the active row at weight 600 where it previously drew Medium — this is the only visible change to the 600, and it is the intended one
how_the_600_instances_get_checked.risk_accepted: Between the two renames the set briefly holds two property vocabularies. Both renames happen in the same synchronous tick, so no render observes the intermediate state. If Figma nonetheless rejects the rename, the script fails before any variant is added and the set is left as it was — the dry run must be read before --apply.
